title: Traces and logs backends: Jaeger, Tempo, Loki
summary: Searching traces by service, operation, attributes and duration; Loki's labels versus structured metadata; LogQL filters; and jumping between signals with trace ids and exemplars.

steps.title: Finding the trace
body: **Jaeger** (2.x is built on the Collector and takes OTLP directly) and **Grafana Tempo** store traces. You search by service,
operation (span name), attributes and duration, then open one trace as a waterfall.
- Jaeger UI: service `shop`, operation `POST /api/checkout`, tags `error=true http.response.status_code=502`, min duration `500ms`.
Its query API v3 answers in OTLP JSON: `GET /api/v3/traces?query.service_name=shop&query.start_time_min=...`.
- Tempo speaks **TraceQL**, which filters on spans inside traces:
```text
{ resource.service.name = "shop" && span.db.system.name = "postgresql" && duration > 50ms }
{ span.http.route = "/api/checkout" && status = error } >> { resource.service.name = "inventory" }
The second finds checkout errors that have an inventory span *below* them (`>>` = descendant).
Trace stores keep days, not months, and usually only sampled traces. So for "how often" questions, use metrics; for "show me one",
traces. Grafana links them: an **exemplar** dot on a latency panel opens its trace; a span's "Logs for this span" button runs a Loki
query by trace id.

steps.prompt: You need checkout traces where an inventory call returned 409. Which TraceQL finds them?
steps.explain: TraceQL selects spans with `{ ... }` and relates them structurally (`>>` descendant, `>` child, `~` sibling). The second is LogQL syntax, the third PromQL.

steps.title: Loki: labels, structured metadata, LogQL
body: Loki indexes only **labels** (a few, low-cardinality: `service_name`, `deployment_environment_name`, `namespace`) and stores the
lines compressed. With OTLP ingestion, resource attributes become labels, and per-record fields (`trace_id`, `span_id`, the
template's attributes) are kept as **structured metadata**: filterable, but not indexed, so they cost nothing in cardinality.
```text
{service_name="shop"}                                     every line of the shop (the stream selector: required)
{service_name="shop"} |= "Reservation failed"            lines containing the text
{service_name="shop"} != "healthz"                       lines not containing it
{service_name="shop"} | trace_id="46ae7e54..."           one request's lines (structured metadata)
{service_name=~"shop|inventory"} | detected_level="error"
sum by (service_name) (count_over_time({service_name=~".+"} | detected_level="error" [5m]))   a metric from logs
Never make a trace id, user id or request path a **label**: each value creates a stream, and Loki slows down and refuses writes
past its stream limits. Same rule as metrics, same reason.

steps.title: A tiny LogQL engine
prompt: Lines are `record LogLine(Dictionary<string, string> Labels, Dictionary<string, string> Meta, string Text);`.
Write `List<string> Run(string query, List<LogLine> lines)` for this subset of LogQL, returning the matching `Text`s in order:
- a stream selector first: `{key="value", key2="value2"}` (every pair must equal a **label**);
- then any number of stages, each separated by spaces:
- `|= "text"`: the line contains the text (case-sensitive); `!= "text"`: it does not;
- `| key="value"`: the line's **label or structured metadata** `key` equals the value.
Parse with `System.Text.RegularExpressions.Regex`. You may assume the query is well formed: values never contain quotes.
solution: bool Field(LogLine l, string k, string v) => (l.Labels.TryGetValue(k, out var a) && a == v) || (l.Meta.TryGetValue(k, out var b) && b == v);
return lines.Where(l => selector.All(p => l.Labels.TryGetValue(p.K, out var x) && x == p.V))
hints: First match the selector at the start (`^\s*\{...\}`), then find the stages in the rest with one regex whose operator group is `\|=|!=|\|` (longest first).
A stage with a key is a field filter; one without is a line filter.
template: LogLine L(string svc, string text, string trace, string level = "info") => new(new() { ["service_name"] = svc }, new() { ["trace_id"] = trace, ["detected_level"] = level }, text);
L("shop", "Order placed for customer 2129 with 1 lines", "aaa"),
L("shop", "Reservation failed for sku 12: stock conflict in warehouse eu-2 (code INV-5821)", "46ae", "error"),
L("shop", "Reservation failed for sku 3: stock conflict in warehouse eu-2 (code INV-5821)", "ccc", "error") };
Dojo.Eq("line filter", new List<string> { dojoLogs[2].Text, dojoLogs[4].Text }, Run("{service_name=\"shop\"} |= \"Reservation failed\"", dojoLogs));
Dojo.Eq("one request's lines, across services? no: the selector picks shop only", new List<string> { dojoLogs[2].Text }, Run("{service_name=\"shop\"} | trace_id=\"46ae\"", dojoLogs));
Dojo.Eq("stages combine", new List<string> { dojoLogs[4].Text }, Run("{service_name=\"shop\"} | detected_level=\"error\" |= \"sku 3\"", dojoLogs));
record LogLine(Dictionary<string, string> Labels, Dictionary<string, string> Meta, string Text);
